blank:0.en: The Manager handed me a form on my first night. Half the boxes had tiny printed labels; the other half were just empty spaces. 'Fill in every *blank*,' he said, then walked away before I could ask what most of them meant. I stared at the paper under the humming lights for a long time.
blank:0.cnHint: 店长递给我一张表格，让我把每个____都填上，然后就走了。
blank:0.hook: One blank asked for something I had never heard of before.
blank:0.line: 'Make sure you fill in every *blank* — the last clerk left three empty.'

reading:0.en: My first slow hour, I found a small shelf behind the register packed with old magazines. Tang caught me flipping through one. 'Night-shift *reading* material,' Tang said with a grin. 'The Manager leaves them. He says a bored clerk makes mistakes.' I put the magazine back, then quietly picked it up again.
reading:0.cnHint: 同事告诉我，店长特意留下杂志给夜班员工当____用。
reading:0.hook: The last page of one magazine had a handwritten note inside.
reading:0.line: 'Good *reading* for slow nights — but hide it when the Manager comes back.'

list:0.en: Tang slid a piece of paper across the counter before heading home. 'This is the regular customers' *list*,' Tang said. 'Learn their faces by Friday.' There were twelve names, each with a note like 'hates plastic bags' or 'always buys two of everything.' I read it three times before my first real customer walked in.
list:0.cnHint: 同事交给我一张顾客____，叮嘱我尽快记住上面的每个人。
list:0.hook: The last name on the list had a small red star next to it.
list:0.line: 'Memorise this *list* before the weekend — trust me, it helps.'

item:0.en: A woman in a long coat came in just after midnight and studied every shelf without picking anything up. Finally she placed a single small eraser on the counter. 'Just this *item*,' she said softly, as if apologising to the store. She paid in exact coins and left without a receipt, disappearing into the dark street.
item:0.cnHint: 一位深夜到访的女士只买了一件____，用硬币付完钱后悄然离去。
item:0.hook: She came back twenty minutes later and stared at the shelf again.
item:0.line: 'Just this one *item*, please — and could you wrap it nicely?'

select:0.en: The Manager spent ten minutes teaching me which eggs to put in the front basket. 'Always *select* the ones with no cracks and a clean shell,' he said, turning each egg slowly in the light. 'A customer who finds a bad egg never forgets it.' I nodded, now afraid to touch a single egg without inspecting it first.
select:0.cnHint: 店长教我如何____出完好无损的鸡蛋摆在篮子前面。
select:0.hook: He then pointed at a crate I was not allowed to open yet.
select:0.line: 'You must *select* only the cleanest ones for the front — no shortcuts.'

need:0.en: Just before 3 a.m. a boy of about ten stood outside the glass door, nose pressed against it. I opened up and asked if he was okay. 'I *need* a candle,' he said in a steady voice. 'The power went out at home and Grandma is scared of the dark.' I found the last one on the bottom shelf and did not charge him.
need:0.cnHint: 一个小男孩深夜来到店里，说他____一根蜡烛，因为奶奶怕黑。
need:0.hook: He thanked me, then asked if we sold batteries too.
need:0.line: 'I *need* a candle right now — it's urgent, please.'

letter:1.en: I stepped outside to pull down the metal shutter a little, and found a folded paper tucked under the door handle. It was a *letter* addressed to the store, written in neat, careful handwriting. No stamp. No return address. Just a name at the bottom I did not recognise.
letter:1.cnHint: 我在店门口发现了一封没有邮票的____，署名陌生。
letter:1.hook: The name at the bottom made the Manager go very still.
letter:1.line: 'There is a *letter* here — and nobody signed it with a real address.'

sheet:1.en: A gust of wind blew down the quiet street just as I stepped out to check the sign above the door. A single white *sheet* of paper spun past my feet, covered in numbers and ticks. It looked like someone's shopping list, or maybe something more important. I picked it up before it could fly away.
sheet:1.cnHint: 一张写满数字的____从街上飘过，我捡了起来。
sheet:1.hook: The last line on that sheet was a time — tonight, midnight.
sheet:1.line: 'This *sheet* was blowing down the street — does it belong to anyone here?'

corresponding:1.en: The store had a small board outside showing today's offers. Each picture had a *corresponding* price tag below it, but someone had swapped two of the tags around as a joke. A child standing on the pavement pointed this out loudly to her mother, laughing. I grabbed a marker and fixed it before the Manager noticed.
corresponding:1.cnHint: 店外展板上的商品图片和____价格标签被人换乱了。
corresponding:1.hook: But the marker I grabbed was not a marker — it was permanent ink.
corresponding:1.line: 'Every picture needs its *corresponding* price tag, or people will complain.'

choose:1.en: Tang stood outside on her break, staring at the row of umbrellas we had placed in a stand by the door for customers to buy. She had been there for three minutes, unable to move. 'It is hard to *choose*,' she told me when I leaned out. 'They are all the same colour, but one of them feels lucky.'
choose:1.cnHint: 同事在门口对着一排雨伞发愁，不知道该____哪一把。
choose:1.hook: She finally picked one — and then the sky immediately cleared.
choose:1.line: 'I need to *choose* carefully — the wrong umbrella brings bad weather energy.'

single:1.en: It was past two in the morning when I noticed a *single* light was still on in the building across the narrow street. Every other window was dark and quiet. Then a figure appeared at that window and looked directly at the store, not moving, for a long moment. I waved. The light went off.
single:1.cnHint: 深夜街对面所有窗户都黑了，只有____一扇还亮着灯。
single:1.hook: The same light came back on exactly one hour later.
single:1.line: 'Not a *single* other window is lit — that one person is watching us.'

line:1.en: I was dragging a crate of drinks through the side door when I saw it: a neat *line* of small stones arranged along the kerb outside, leading from the lamp post to our entrance, as if someone had left a trail. Each stone was about the same size. Tang said it had not been there at midnight. Nobody saw who made it.
line:1.cnHint: 店门外的路边多了一条用小石子排成的____，不知是谁放的。
line:1.hook: The line of stones pointed directly at the back wall of the store.
line:1.line: 'Someone made a *line* of stones outside — it goes straight to our door.'

become:1.en: The street outside was empty and pale under the lamp light when an elderly man sat down on the low wall opposite. He opened a small bag, took out a folded board, and began to set up a chess game by himself. It had *become* his nightly habit, Tang told me later — rain or shine, same wall, same time.
become:1.cnHint: 街对面有位老人，每天深夜独自下棋，这已经____他的习惯了。
become:1.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he looked up and gestured for a partner.
become:1.line: 'It has *become* normal to see him out there — but he never invites anyone.'

centre:1.en: Just outside our door, someone had chalked a large circle on the pavement, with a bold X at the *centre*. Kids from the afternoon shift had probably drawn it. But at three in the morning, a very serious man in a coat stepped off the bus, walked straight to the X, and stood on it, checking his watch.
centre:1.cnHint: 店门外地上有人用粉笔画了个圈，一个男人深夜径直走向____站定。
centre:1.hook: He looked up at the store sign, then said one quiet word into his phone.
centre:1.line: 'Stand at the *centre* of the circle and do not move — I will find you.'

passage:0.en: The Manager handed me a short *passage* from the store manual and told me to read it before my shift began. It described the narrow walk between the drink coolers and the back wall — the only way to reach the stock room. I read it twice, then looked up. The path was already blocked by a tower of boxes.
passage:0.cnHint: 店长让我读手册里的一____，上面描述了通往库房的唯一通道。
passage:0.hook: Behind the boxes, something quietly moved.
passage:0.line: 'Read this *passage* carefully — it tells you where everything is.'

base:0.en: I found a small shelf unit lying on its side near the entrance. Its *base* was cracked, and someone had tried to fix it with a thick strip of tape. The Manager said nothing when I pointed at it, just handed me more tape. I added three more strips. The shelf still leaned a little, like it was listening.
base:0.cnHint: 货架底部____坏了，店长只是递给我更多胶带。
base:0.hook: Then I noticed the shelf was hiding a small locked box.
base:0.line: 'The *base* is broken, but it will hold if you are gentle.'

section:0.en: The snack *section* took up the whole left wall, and every item had a handwritten price tag in the Manager's thin, careful letters. My job was to check each tag before dawn. Tang warned me that one tag was always missing — the same one, every single night. Nobody knew who kept taking it.
section:0.cnHint: 零食____的价格标签每晚都会少一张，没人知道是谁拿走的。
section:0.hook: Tonight, I planned to find out.
section:0.line: 'Check every item in the snack *section* before three o'clock.'

answer:0.en: A customer asked me where the hot drinks were. Simple question. But my mind went completely blank. I looked left, then right, then left again. Tang walked past, tapped the counter twice, and pointed without looking up. The customer nodded and walked away. I still did not give a single *answer* myself.
answer:0.cnHint: 顾客问我热饮在哪里，我完全不知道如何____。
answer:0.hook: Tang gave me a look I could not quite read.
answer:0.line: 'You will need a faster *answer* than that next time.'

study:0.en: Between customers, I found a quiet corner behind the register and opened my English notebook. The Manager had a small *study* area tucked under the stairs — just a chair, a lamp, and a shelf — and he said I could use it on slow nights. Tonight was slow. My pen barely moved.
study:0.cnHint: 店长在楼梯下有一间小____，他说我可以在空闲时使用。
study:0.hook: On the shelf sat a photo I was not meant to see.
study:0.line: 'Use the *study* when it is quiet — I will not mind.'

mark:0.en: Tang showed me how to date the fresh sandwiches by pressing a small ink stamp onto each wrapper. 'Every *mark* tells the customer how long it has been sitting here,' she said. I pressed too hard the first time and the date bled into a dark smudge. Tang laughed, just a little.
mark:0.cnHint: 唐教我在三明治包装上盖日期____，我第一次用力过猛。
mark:0.hook: One sandwich had no mark at all.
mark:0.line: 'Each *mark* must be clear — blurry ones cause real trouble.'

choice:0.en: The drink cooler had six shelves, and restocking it was my first real task. The Manager said I had a *choice*: follow the map taped to the inside of the cooler door, or guess. I stared at the map. It was drawn in pencil and half of it had been rubbed away. I guessed.
choice:0.cnHint: 补货时店长说我有____：照地图来，或者自己猜。
choice:0.hook: By morning, three drinks were definitely in the wrong place.
choice:0.line: 'It is your *choice*, but the map is there for a reason.'

part:0.en: Just before two in the morning, the lights above the bread rack flickered. Tang said that fixing the lights was not our *part* of the job — that belonged to the day crew. So we placed an extra lamp on the floor instead. Its warm glow made the bread look almost golden. A customer stopped and stared, surprised.
part:0.cnHint: 面包架上的灯坏了，但修灯不是我们____的工作。
part:0.hook: The customer bought every last loaf.
part:0.line: 'Fixing lights is not our *part* — call the day crew.'

passage:1.en: My first night shift began outside, under the yellow lamp above the door. The Manager pointed to the narrow *passage* between the store and the wall, where delivery boxes were stacked. 'Learn where everything lives before you touch the register,' he said. I nodded, already wondering what else was hiding back there.
passage:1.cnHint: 店长让我先熟悉门旁那条堆满箱子的____，再去收银台。
passage:1.hook: Something behind the boxes moved — and it wasn't the wind.
passage:1.line: 'The *passage* is narrow, so stack the smaller boxes on top.'

base:1.en: The Manager showed me the supply shelf on my first night. 'This store is the *base* for three delivery drivers,' he said, tapping the lowest shelf with his pen. 'They sleep in their vans outside and restock here at dawn.' I looked through the glass door and counted three vans I hadn't noticed before.
base:1.cnHint: 店长告诉我，这家店是三名快递员补给的____。
base:1.hook: One of the vans had its light on at two in the morning.
base:1.line: 'Think of this shelf as our *base* — everything starts from here.'

section:1.en: Tang walked me through the store before the rush. 'Hot drinks, cold drinks, snacks — each *section* has its own restocking order,' she said, handing me a clipboard. I wrote it all down carefully. But when I looked up, a teenage boy was quietly moving a bag of chips from one shelf to another, watching my reaction.
section:1.cnHint: 同事唐带我熟悉店里每个商品____的补货顺序。
section:1.hook: The boy smiled at me like he had done this a hundred times before.
section:1.line: 'Never mix items — every *section* has its own place on the clipboard.'

answer:1.en: A woman knocked on the glass door at midnight and held up a small card. I opened the door and she asked, 'Do you carry that warm barley tea?' My *answer* was honest: I didn't know yet. She laughed softly and said she'd wait while I checked. She came every Tuesday, I'd later learn, and always asked something I didn't know.
answer:1.cnHint: 一位女士深夜敲门问我有没有麦茶，我不得不如实给出____。
answer:1.hook: She was already halfway down the street before I found it.
answer:1.line: 'Your *answer* was honest — I respect that more than a quick lie.'

study:1.en: It was quiet at three in the morning when a young man spread his books across the small table by the window. 'Is it okay if I *study* here for a bit?' he asked, looking embarrassed. I said sure and brought him a hot tea without charging him. He left a sticky note on the table that said 'thank you' in four languages.
study:1.cnHint: 凌晨三点，一个年轻人问能否在靠窗小桌旁____一会儿。
study:1.hook: The next night, there were two of them at the table.
study:1.line: 'I always *study* better here than in the library — it's warmer.'

mark:1.en: Tang pointed to a small red *mark* on the floor near the entrance. 'Stand here when it's slow — you can see the whole store and the street at once,' she said. I thought it was a strange thing to memorize. Then, at four in the morning, I understood exactly why she had told me.
mark:1.cnHint: 唐告诉我，地上那个红色的____是夜班最佳站立位。
mark:1.hook: A figure had been standing outside that same spot for twenty minutes.
mark:1.line: 'See that *mark*? That's your best spot on a quiet night.'

choice:1.en: At two in the morning a man stood in front of the drinks fridge for a long time. 'Tough *choice*?' I called over. He turned, surprised, then grinned. 'My wife wants cold tea. My mother wants warm soup. I only have two hands.' I helped him find a small bag for both. He looked so relieved that I felt like I'd solved something important.
choice:1.cnHint: 一位男士在饮料柜前犹豫不决，难以做出____。
choice:1.hook: He came back an hour later — alone, this time, and in a hurry.
choice:1.line: 'It's a tough *choice* when everyone at home wants something different.'

part:1.en: On my first night, the Manager said the hardest *part* of the job was not the late hours — it was learning to read the street outside. 'Every person who walks past that window at three in the morning has a reason,' he said, pulling on his coat. He left without explaining further, and I spent the rest of the shift watching the window.
part:1.cnHint: 店长说，这份工作最难的____不是熬夜，而是学会观察街道。
part:1.hook: At three fifteen, a woman stopped outside and stared at her own reflection.
part:1.line: 'The hardest *part* is not the hours — it's learning to read people.'

bank:0.en: The Manager showed me the storage room on my first night. One whole shelf held nothing but instant noodle cups — a *bank* of flavours so large I counted twelve varieties. 'Regulars have strong opinions,' she warned me. I smiled politely. Outside, someone was already rattling the front door.
bank:0.cnHint: 店长向我展示了储藏室里庞大的方便面____，足足有十二种口味。
bank:0.hook: Whoever was at the door had not come for noodles.
bank:0.line: 'We keep a *bank* of every flavour — run out of one and someone will complain all week.'

statement:0.en: Tang handed me a printed sheet during handover. 'This is the till *statement* from last night,' he said, circling a number in red pen. 'One item sold, no record of payment.' He looked at me with calm, curious eyes — as if the mystery delighted him more than it worried him.
statement:0.cnHint: 阿糖给我看了昨晚收银机的____，上面有一笔奇怪的未记录销售。
statement:0.hook: The item that vanished from stock was not on any shelf.
statement:0.line: 'Check the till *statement* before you close — last week it caught something odd.'

identify:0.en: A regular came in at two in the morning wearing a hood pulled low. I tried to *identify* him by his order — three cans of corn soup and a single birthday candle — but nothing clicked. He paid in exact coins, nodded once, and walked back into the rain.
identify:0.cnHint: 我试图通过他奇怪的购物清单来____这位神秘的蒙面常客。
identify:0.hook: He bought a birthday candle, but whose birthday was it?
identify:0.line: 'Can you *identify* that man? He comes every Thursday — same order, never speaks.'

comprehension:0.en: The register manual was twelve pages long and full of words I had never seen. My *comprehension* of the whole system hovered somewhere near zero. Tang watched me stare at the screen, then laughed softly and flipped to page three. 'Just this part,' he said. 'The rest is for emergencies.'
comprehension:0.cnHint: 我对收银机操作手册的____几乎为零，幸好阿糖帮我翻到了最有用的那页。
comprehension:0.hook: I wondered what kind of emergency would need the other nine pages.
comprehension:0.line: 'Your *comprehension* will improve fast — the night shift teaches you everything in one week.'

require:0.en: A woman in a long coat came in and spent five minutes reading the label on a bottle of vitamin water. 'Does this *require* refrigeration after opening?' she asked without looking up. I checked the back of the bottle, then nodded. She put it down and bought hot tea instead. She did this, Tang later told me, every single night.
require:0.cnHint: 一位常客每晚都来问某种饮料是否____冷藏，然后每次都选择买热茶。
require:0.hook: Tang said she had never once taken the tea home unopened.
require:0.line: 'Some items *require* a little patience from the staff — she is testing you, not the label.'

least:0.en: Lin came in from the store across the street, pretending to shop. She picked up a rice ball, put it back, then checked our coffee machine with narrowed eyes. 'Your prices are at *least* five percent lower than ours,' she said, almost to herself. I smiled and offered her a free paper cup. She took it without a word.
least:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林发现我们的价格至____比她店里低5%，表情很是复杂。
least:0.hook: She left the cup on the counter, still full and still steaming.
least:0.line: 'You charge at *least* ten cents less per cup — the Manager will hear about this.'

following:0.en: The Manager left me a sticky note listing rules for my first solo hour. The *following* three were underlined twice: never leave the counter empty, always greet a customer first, and trust the coffee machine only after it beeps twice. I memorised all three before she reached the door. She turned back anyway to check.
following:0.cnHint: 店长在便利贴上列出了____几条规定，其中三条还被画了双下划线。
following:0.hook: There was a fourth rule she did not write down.
following:0.line: 'Remember the *following*: if the lights flicker, do not touch the old fridge in the corner.'

decide:0.en: At four in the morning, a sleepy student stood in front of the snack wall for ten full minutes. He could not *decide* between cheese crackers and seaweed chips. I waited. He sighed. He picked up both, looked at his wallet, and put one back — the wrong one, by the look on his face.
decide:0.cnHint: 一个困倦的学生在零食墙前花了十分钟也无法____买哪种小吃。
decide:0.hook: He came back three minutes later and swapped them in silence.
decide:0.line: 'I always *decide* on the cheese ones and then regret it — do you have any samples?'

letter:0.en: The Manager handed me a small envelope on my first night. 'Read this before your shift ends,' he said. Inside was a single *letter* — not an email, not a note, but a proper, handwritten one — from the clerk I was replacing. It listed every regular customer by nickname and their usual order.
letter:0.cnHint: 店长给了我一封____，里面是前任店员留下的顾客信息。
letter:0.hook: The last line of the letter said: 'Watch out for the umbrella man.'
letter:0.line: 'I wrote you a *letter* — some things are better said by hand.'

sheet:0.en: Tang slid a *sheet* of paper across the counter before clocking out. Every row had a time, a product name, and a number. 'Restock list,' she said, already pulling on her coat. 'Finish it before four or the Manager will know.' The columns were neat, but one item was circled three times in red pen.
sheet:0.cnHint: 阿糖留给我一张____，上面写满了补货任务，其中一项被红笔圈了三次。
sheet:0.hook: The circled item was marked 'do NOT order more — ask me why tomorrow.'
sheet:0.line: 'Here is the *sheet* — every item the night shift needs to check.'

corresponding:0.en: The Manager showed me the shelf map on my first hour. Each product had a number, and each number had a *corresponding* spot on the shelves marked with a small sticker. 'Match the number, find the spot, done,' he said. Simple enough — until I noticed one sticker had been peeled off and stuck back upside down.
corresponding:0.cnHint: 店长向我解释了货架地图，每个商品编号都有____的位置标签。
corresponding:0.hook: Someone had moved that product on purpose, and recently.
corresponding:0.line: 'Find the number, then find its *corresponding* spot on the shelf.'

choose:0.en: A tired student came in just before midnight and stood in front of the snack wall for a full five minutes. I watched him *choose*, put something back, choose again, then look at me helplessly. 'It is two in the morning and I cannot decide,' he said. I handed him the cheaper one. He looked relieved. He paid and left without a word.
choose:0.cnHint: 一个学生在零食墙前犹豫很久，无法____，最后我帮他做了决定。
choose:0.hook: He came back twenty minutes later and bought the other one too.
choose:0.line: 'I cannot *choose* — they both look good and I am so tired.'

single:0.en: An old woman came in every night, Tang had warned me. She always bought one item. Tonight it was a *single* small carton of warm milk, which she held in both hands like something precious. She did not speak, just nodded at me and left. The bell above the door rang softly twice — once going out, once, somehow, a moment later.
single:0.cnHint: 一位老太太每晚只买____件东西，今晚是一盒热牛奶，她走后门铃响了两次。
single:0.hook: There was no second customer behind her — the door had not opened again.
single:0.line: 'Just a *single* carton of milk, please — the warm kind.'

line:0.en: Tang showed me the queue system on slow nights: a strip of yellow tape on the floor marked where customers should stand. 'One *line*, no crowding, everyone calm,' she said. By two in the morning the store was empty and the tape looked almost funny — a line for nobody. Then the door opened and three people walked in together.
line:0.cnHint: 阿糖教我用地板上的黄色胶带维持一条排队的____，但深夜无人时它显得有些可笑。
line:0.hook: All three of them stepped over the tape without looking at it, like they had done it before.
line:0.line: 'Stand behind the *line* on the floor — it keeps things orderly.'

become:0.en: The Manager told me the store had *become* a kind of shelter for the street. 'In winter, people come in just to get warm,' he said. 'Let them stand. Do not rush them.' I had thought it was just a shop. After my first night, I was not so sure. Every face that came through the door seemed to carry something heavier than whatever they came to buy.
become:0.cnHint: 店长说这家便利店已经____了街上人们的某种庇护所，不只是一家普通商店。
become:0.hook: He said this very quietly, looking at a corner of the shop I had not noticed yet.
become:0.line: 'This place has *become* more than a store — you will see soon.'

centre:0.en: The Manager pointed to the round mat at the entrance. 'Stand near the *centre* of the mat when you greet people,' he said. 'It looks welcoming.' I tried it. It felt strange at first, like being on a small stage. But the third customer of the night smiled at me as she walked in, and the feeling changed completely.
centre:0.cnHint: 店长让我站在门口垫子的____迎接顾客，第三位顾客的微笑让我感受到了其中的意义。
centre:0.hook: That third customer paused, looked back once, and said, 'You must be new — he left, then?'

blank:1.en: I stood outside the store at eleven p.m., staring at the staff schedule pinned to the door. My name was there, but the hours column beside it was a *blank* — someone had forgotten to write them in. I had no idea if my shift had already started or not.
blank:1.cnHint: 我盯着门口的排班表，发现自己名字旁边的时间栏是个____。
blank:1.hook: The door swung open before I could decide.
blank:1.line: 'There is a *blank* where your hours should be,' the Manager said, frowning.

reading:1.en: I found Tang sitting on the front step under the yellow lamp, a folded magazine open on her knees. She looked up, surprised. 'Night shift?' she asked. I nodded. She smiled and held up her *reading*. 'Good. I always need someone to talk to when the street goes quiet.'
reading:1.cnHint: 同事坐在台阶上，手里拿着她的____，笑着跟我打招呼。
reading:1.hook: Then she turned to a page with a circled name.
reading:1.line: 'This *reading* has kept me company every slow night,' Tang said softly.

list:1.en: Outside, a handwritten *list* was taped beside the delivery door — milk, buns, batteries, three kinds of instant noodles. At the bottom someone had added, in much smaller letters, 'do not forget the cat food.' I looked around. I had not known there was a cat.
list:1.cnHint: 送货门旁边贴着一张____，最下面有人用小字加了一行字。
list:1.hook: Something soft brushed my ankle in the dark.
list:1.line: 'Check the *list* before you sign anything,' the Manager called from inside.

item:1.en: The Manager handed me a paper before I even stepped through the door. 'Every *item* on that sheet must be counted before midnight,' he said. There were thirty-two lines. I glanced at the quiet street, took a breath, and walked in, wondering which shelf to start with.
item:1.cnHint: 店长递给我一张纸，要求我在午夜前清点上面每一个____。
item:1.hook: Line twenty-nine had no product name, only a question mark.
item:1.line: 'Each *item* must match the number on the shelf,' the Manager said firmly.

select:1.en: Tang pointed to a small crate of fruit by the entrance. 'We *select* the best ones and move them to the front each evening,' she explained. 'The rest go to the back.' She made it sound simple, but every orange looked exactly the same to me in the pale street light.
select:1.cnHint: 同事告诉我，每天傍晚都要从水果箱里____出最好看的摆在前面。
select:1.hook: One orange at the bottom was warm — far too warm.
select:1.line: 'You *select* the nicest ones first, always,' Tang said with a wink.

need:1.en: I was still outside, checking my phone for the store's entry code, when a small boy ran up and pressed his face against the glass. 'Are you open?' he called. 'I *need* to buy something right now.' He was maybe eight years old and completely out of breath.
need:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩跑到橱窗边，气喘吁吁地说他____买一样东西。
need:1.hook: He held up a crumpled note with a single word on it.
need:1.line: 'I *need* it before my mum gets home, please,' the boy said breathlessly.

bank:1.en: On my way to the store for my first night shift, I passed the old *bank* on the corner. Its stone steps were cold under the lamp. A man sat on them, staring at a small notebook. He looked up as I passed, then quickly tucked the notebook away.
bank:1.cnHint: 我去上第一个夜班的路上，经过街角的____，台阶上坐着一个盯着笔记本的陌生男人。
bank:1.hook: The notebook had our store's address written on the cover.
bank:1.line: 'This *bank* has been closed for ten years,' he said softly.

statement:1.en: Just before I unlocked the store door, an older woman pressed a folded paper into my hand. 'Give this to the Manager,' she said, then walked away fast. I opened it inside. It was a single typed *statement* saying the store owed her a debt from three years ago.
statement:1.cnHint: 我刚到店门口，一位老太太塞给我一张写着____的纸，要我转交给店长。
statement:1.hook: The Manager's face went pale the moment he read it.
statement:1.line: 'That *statement* is every word true,' she called back without turning.

identify:1.en: A delivery truck stopped outside, and the driver leaned out. He held up a blurry photo and asked me to *identify* the person in it. The face was half hidden by a hood, standing right in front of our store window. I looked at the photo, then slowly looked at the window.
identify:1.cnHint: 送货司机拿着一张模糊的照片，请我____照片里站在店门口的那个人。
identify:1.hook: The figure in the photo was wearing my exact jacket.
identify:1.line: 'Can you *identify* anyone in this picture?' he asked, watching my face.

comprehension:1.en: Tang handed me a thick binder on my first night. 'Store rules,' he said cheerfully. I flipped through forty pages of tiny text. My *comprehension* of Chinese store policy was, at that moment, close to zero. Tang watched me struggle and simply said, 'Don't worry. The regulars will teach you.'
comprehension:1.cnHint: 同事递给我厚厚一本店规，我对内容的____几乎为零，他说常客会教我的。
comprehension:1.hook: One regular was already watching me through the glass door.
comprehension:1.line: 'Your *comprehension* will improve by morning,' Tang said with a grin.

require:1.en: The Manager met me outside before my shift and walked me around the block. 'This job will *require* patience,' he said, stopping at each spot where something had once gone wrong. A broken lamp post. A cracked bench. A faded chalk mark on the pavement. He never explained any of them.
require:1.cnHint: 店长带我在街区转了一圈，说这份工作____耐心，却对路上每个奇怪的地方只字不提。
require:1.hook: The chalk mark was shaped like a small arrow pointing at our door.
require:1.line: 'We *require* every new clerk to see this before their first shift,' he said quietly.

following:1.en: A handwritten note was taped to the staff door when I arrived. It listed the *following* instructions in neat capital letters: unlock at midnight, leave the back light off, and do not ask about the blue box under the counter. There was no name at the bottom.
following:1.cnHint: 员工门上贴着一张便条，写着____几条指示，其中一条是不许询问柜台下那个蓝盒子。
following:1.hook: The blue box was already gone when I looked under the counter.
following:1.line: 'The *following* rules were written by the last night clerk,' Tang said carefully.

decide:1.en: I stood at the corner for a full minute before my shift, trying to *decide* whether the light above the store sign was flickering or just blinking on purpose. A girl passing by stopped beside me, stared up at it, and said, 'It started doing that the night Lin arrived.'
decide:1.cnHint: 我盯着店招牌上方的灯出神，试图____它是在故障还是故意闪烁，路过的女孩提到了林。
decide:1.hook: Lin was standing behind me before I could turn around.
decide:1.line: 'You have to *decide* quickly on this street,' the girl said, then left.

passage:2.en: Behind the snack shelves, I found a narrow *passage* leading to a back room. A single bulb hung from the ceiling. Old delivery boxes lined both walls. Someone had left a warm cup of tea on a crate near the door — and it was still steaming.
passage:2.cnHint: 我在货架后发现了一条通向后室的____，里面有人留下了一杯热茶。
passage:2.hook: Nobody on the schedule had come in that night.
passage:2.line: 'There is a *passage* behind the shelves — did the Manager show you?'

base:2.en: The Manager pointed to a tall display stand near the window. 'Always check the *base* first,' he said. 'Things fall and hide down there.' I looked — sure enough, a small envelope was wedged beneath it, with my name written on the front.
base:2.cnHint: 店长让我检查展示架的____，我在那里发现了一个写着我名字的信封。
base:2.hook: Inside the envelope was a single key.
base:2.line: 'Check the *base* of every stand before your shift ends.'

section:2.en: Tang had organised the drinks fridge into neat groups. 'This *section* is for hot cans,' she said, tapping the right side. Then she paused and frowned. One can was ice-cold and faced backwards — as if someone had put it there on purpose, hiding the label.
section:2.cnHint: 阿糖向我介绍饮料柜的热饮____时，发现有一罐饮料被故意反放着。
section:2.hook: The label on the back read a single handwritten word.
section:2.line: 'This *section* is mine to manage — please do not move anything.'

answer:2.en: A regular came in just after midnight, bought nothing, and slid a folded note across the counter. Inside was a maths problem, nothing more. I stared at it for ten minutes before writing my *answer* on the back and leaving it by the register. He never returned for it.
answer:2.cnHint: 一位常客留下了一道数学题，我写下____后，他却再也没回来取。
answer:2.hook: The problem was not really about maths.
answer:2.line: 'My *answer* is on the note — you can check it yourself.'

study:2.en: Lin came in with a thick textbook under her arm. She set it on the counter and ordered black coffee. 'Late *study* session,' she said with a tired smile. I noticed her bookmark was in the very last page. She had almost finished — but her eyes looked worried, not proud.
study:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带着课本来买咖啡，说是来____的，但她的眼神看起来很担忧。
study:2.hook: She glanced at the door three times before sitting down.
study:2.line: 'Another night of *study* — the exam is closer than I thought.'

mark:2.en: Near the end of my first shift, I noticed a small red *mark* on the back wall, about shoulder height. It looked like a paint scratch, but it was shaped too neatly — almost like an arrow pointing toward the floor vent below it.
mark:2.cnHint: 我在后墙上发现了一个红色____，形状像一支箭头，指向地板通风口。
mark:2.hook: The vent cover had been removed and replaced very recently.
mark:2.line: 'That *mark* on the wall — was it there when you started tonight?'

choice:2.en: The Manager left me alone at two in the morning with a simple instruction: 'If a stranger asks to use the back room, it is your *choice*.' I had no idea what that meant. An hour later, a woman in a wet coat knocked on the side door and waited without saying a word.
choice:2.cnHint: 店长说后室是否借给陌生人，由我____决定，一小时后真的来了一位陌生人。
choice:2.hook: She already knew exactly where the side door was.
choice:2.line: 'It is your *choice*, but choose quickly — the rain is heavy.'

part:2.en: Tang showed me the stock list before she left. 'Learn the frozen *part* first,' she said, circling a section of the shelf map. 'It changes every night.' I looked at the map closely. Someone had already circled the same section in a different colour — long before I arrived.
part:2.cnHint: 阿糖让我先熟悉库存的冷冻____，但我发现地图上早已有人用不同颜色圈出了同一区域。
part:2.hook: The second circle was drawn in the same pen as my name tag.
part:2.line: 'The frozen *part* is tricky — count it twice, always.'

blank:2.en: The Manager handed me a printed form before my first shift. Most of it was filled in, but one line near the bottom was empty. 'Write your name in the *blank*,' he said. I picked up the pen and, for some reason, paused. That small white space suddenly felt like the start of something much bigger.
blank:2.cnHint: 店长让我在表格的____处填上名字，我拿起笔，却莫名地停顿了一下。
blank:2.hook: The Manager watched my hand with a look I could not quite read.
blank:2.line: 'Just write your name in the *blank* and we can get started.'

reading:2.en: Near the end of the shelf by the window, someone had left a thin paperback face-down between the magazines. I picked it up. Inside the front cover, in small handwriting, it said: 'For late nights when the world is quiet.' A *reading* for the sleepless, I thought. I put it back carefully.
reading:2.cnHint: 我在杂志架旁发现一本薄薄的书，扉页上写着留给深夜____者的话。
reading:2.hook: The handwriting looked surprisingly like Tang's.
reading:2.line: 'This kind of *reading* is the best thing about a quiet night shift.'

list:2.en: Taped to the inside of the storage room door was a long piece of paper. At the top, someone had written: 'Things the night shift must never forget.' Below it was a neat *list* of twelve items, each one ticked except the last. Number twelve just said: 'Check the back corner. Always.' I had no idea what that meant.
list:2.cnHint: 储藏室门上贴着一张____，最后一条没有打勾，只写着"永远检查后角落"。
list:2.hook: Nobody had told me what was in that back corner.
list:2.line: 'I wrote that *list* on my first night — you should probably read it.'

item:2.en: I was counting the snacks on the middle shelf when I noticed something strange. Every *item* on the row was turned so its label faced the back wall instead of the aisle. All of them. In a perfectly straight line. Someone had done it on purpose, and done it very recently, because the shelf had been fine an hour ago.
item:2.cnHint: 我发现货架上每一____商品的标签都朝向墙壁，显然是刚刚有人故意为之。
item:2.hook: The store camera above that shelf had been turned slightly sideways.
item:2.line: 'Every *item* on that shelf was flipped — did you see who did it?'

select:2.en: Tang showed me the staff discount card on my first break. 'You can only use it to *select* drinks and snacks,' she said, sliding it across the counter. 'The Manager marks the ones that count.' She pointed to a small green dot on certain price tags. I looked around the store and noticed the green dots formed an odd pattern on the wall.
select:2.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我员工折扣卡只能用于____特定的饮料和零食，我却发现绿色标签排成了奇怪的图案。
select:2.hook: The green dots, I now saw, spelled a single short word.
select:2.line: 'You can only *select* the ones with the green dot — those are the rules.'

need:2.en: Around two in the morning a woman came in, looked straight at me, and said: 'I *need* the thing.' I stared. She added nothing. She just stood there, calm and patient, as though I already knew exactly what she meant. After a long moment she smiled, walked to the far refrigerator, and pulled out a small bottle of warm honey water.
need:2.cnHint: 凌晨两点，一位女士走进来说她____"那个东西"，却没有进一步解释。
need:2.hook: She paid and left, but she had been here before — I was certain of it.
need:2.line: 'I *need* the thing — you know the one, the one in the back fridge.'

letter:2.en: My first task tonight was sorting the mail shelf near the door. Most envelopes held bills, but one small *letter* had no address — just a name written in careful handwriting: 'Tang.' I set it apart on the counter. An hour later, Tang arrived for the early shift, saw it, and went very quiet.
letter:2.cnHint: 我在整理货架时发现了一封写着同事名字的神秘____。
letter:2.hook: Tang read it twice, then hid it quickly inside a jacket pocket.
letter:2.line: 'There is a *letter* here with your name on it,' I said, sliding it across the counter.

sheet:2.en: The Manager had left me a single *sheet* of paper on the register: a hand-drawn map of every shelf, with each product's spot numbered in red pen. It was surprisingly detailed — even the location of the spare mop was marked. I felt oddly moved by how much care had gone into it.
sheet:2.cnHint: 店长给我留了一____手绘的商品位置图，帮我熟悉夜班工作。
sheet:2.hook: At the bottom of the sheet, a note read: 'Do NOT open the back room on your own.'
sheet:2.line: 'Use this *sheet* as your guide tonight — every item has its place,' the Manager had written.

corresponding:2.en: The Manager had built a colour-coded stock list: each shelf had a number, and every product had a *corresponding* sticker in a matching colour. It was clever, but someone had switched two stickers as a joke. I spent twenty minutes finding the mistake before the morning delivery arrived.
corresponding:2.cnHint: 我发现有人把货架标签和____的颜色贴纸调换了位置，捣了个小乱。
corresponding:2.hook: Only Lin, smiling too innocently outside the window, could have done it.
corresponding:2.line: 'Each sticker has a *corresponding* shelf number — match them before the delivery,' the Manager had warned.

choose:2.en: A young woman stood in front of the drink cooler for a full five minutes, unable to *choose* between two bottles. She read every label twice, held them both up to the light, and sighed. I offered to flip a coin. She laughed, took the one on the left, and said it was always the one on the left anyway.
choose:2.cnHint: 一位顾客在饮料柜前站了很久，迟迟无法____该买哪瓶饮料。
choose:2.hook: She came back ten minutes later and stared at the cooler again.
choose:2.line: 'I always *choose* the one on the left — it just feels right,' she said with a small laugh.

single:2.en: At 2 a.m. a man came in and placed a *single* coin on the counter without a word. He pointed at the cheapest cup of instant noodles on the shelf. The coin was exactly the right amount. I handed over the noodles, and he nodded once before walking back out into the dark street.
single:2.cnHint: 深夜有位男士只放了一枚____硬币，恰好够买一碗泡面。
single:2.hook: The next night, the same coin — I was sure of it — appeared on the counter again.
single:2.line: 'Just this one — a *single* coin is all I have tonight,' he said quietly, not meeting my eyes.

line:2.en: Just before three in the morning, a short *line* formed at my register — four people, all buying the same triangle rice snack. They did not know each other. Each one paid, nodded, and left without a word. I looked at the shelf; only one rice snack remained. I ate it myself on my break.
line:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，四个互不相识的顾客排成一____，买的东西竟然完全一样。
line:2.hook: The last customer paused at the door and said, 'She recommended it to me.'
line:2.line: 'There is a *line* forming — I will be quick,' the man at the back called out with a tired smile.

become:2.en: Tang told me that the store had once been a flower shop. 'It *became* a convenience store ten years ago,' she said, wiping down the counter, 'but on rainy nights, I still smell roses.' I laughed, but then the rain started, and I was not so sure she was joking.
become:2.cnHint: 同事告诉我，这家便利店曾经____过另一种完全不同的店。
become:2.hook: Under the counter I later found one dried rose, pressed flat and very old.
become:2.line: 'This place *became* a store ten years ago, but it still holds its old secrets,' Tang said softly.

centre:2.en: The Manager had placed a tall stand of snacks right at the *centre* of the store, blocking the view from the register to the door. Every time a customer walked in, I had to lean sideways to see them. By midnight I had developed a small but reliable lean to the left.
centre:2.cnHint: 店长把一个零食架放在店铺____，让我从收银台完全看不到门口。
centre:2.hook: Lin texted me: 'He moves it every week — just wait.'
centre:2.line: 'I put it at the *centre* so customers see it first — good for sales,' the Manager explained cheerfully.

bank:2.en: The Manager left me a note taped to the register: check the snack *bank* before midnight and restock anything below ten units. I counted chips, crackers, and dried mango. Everything looked fine — until I opened the bottom drawer and found it completely empty except for one very old sticky note.
bank:2.cnHint: 店长留了张纸条，让我在午夜前检查零食____，但最底层的抽屉里藏着意想不到的东西。
bank:2.hook: The sticky note had a name on it — and it was not the Manager's.
bank:2.line: 'Check the snack *bank* every night — the bottom drawer is the important one.'

statement:2.en: A folded paper fell out of a returned umbrella near the door. It looked like a bank *statement*, rows of small numbers printed in neat columns. Someone had circled one line in red pen and written 'WHY?' beside it. I set it on the lost-and-found shelf and tried not to wonder.
statement:2.cnHint: 一把被遗忘的雨伞里掉出一张____，上面有人用红笔圈出了一行数字。
statement:2.hook: Twenty minutes later, someone tried the door but did not come in.
statement:2.line: 'That *statement* has been in the umbrella for a week — nobody claimed it yet.'

identify:2.en: A delivery arrived at 2 a.m. with no store name on the box, only a string of numbers. I tried to *identify* which shelf it belonged to by checking the product code list the Manager had taped inside the stockroom door, but the code was not on the list at all.
identify:2.cnHint: 深夜到货的包裹没有店名，我试图____它属于哪个货架，但编号根本不在清单上。
identify:2.hook: Tang arrived early and went pale the moment they saw the box.
identify:2.line: 'Can you *identify* the product code? It should match the list on the door.'

comprehension:2.en: The instruction sheet for the new card reader was four pages long and printed in a font so small I needed to squint. My *comprehension* of the first page took ten full minutes. By page three I had given up and simply pressed every button in order until it beeped happily.
comprehension:2.cnHint: 新刷卡机的说明书字体极小，我对第一页的____花了整整十分钟，最后只好乱按按钮。
comprehension:2.hook: The receipt it printed had someone else's name at the top.
comprehension:2.line: 'My *comprehension* of this manual is zero — did you actually read it?'

require:2.en: A quiet woman asked if the store could hold a package for her neighbour. I checked the small sign the Manager had posted: 'All held items *require* a written note with a phone number.' I told her this politely. She nodded, wrote the note, and slid it across the counter without a word.
require:2.cnHint: 一位女士想让我代收包裹，但店长的规定____留下书面联系方式，她一言不发地写好递了过来。
require:2.hook: The phone number she wrote was the store's own number.
require:2.line: 'The rules *require* a phone number — just a quick note is fine.'

following:2.en: The Manager left a checklist for the night shift. The *following* tasks were written in careful order: wipe the counter, count the till, lock the back door, water the small plant by the window. I did them all. The plant, it turned out, was plastic.
following:2.cnHint: 店长留下了值夜班的清单，____几项任务写得井井有条，但最后一项让我出了洋相。
following:2.hook: Underneath the plant was a tiny key I had never noticed before.
following:2.line: 'Please do the *following* things before six — the list is on the fridge.'

decide:2.en: Two chocolate bars sat in the lost-and-found box, unclaimed for a week. I could not *decide* whether to throw them away or eat them, so I left a small note: 'Owner — please collect by Friday.' On Friday morning they were gone, but the note had a new line added in different handwriting.
decide:2.cnHint: 失物招领箱里有两块无人认领的巧克力，我无法____该怎么处理，周五早上它们不见了，但留言条上多了一行字。
decide:2.hook: The new line said: 'Thank you. Same time next week.'
decide:2.line: 'You have to *decide* before Friday — after that the rules say we clear the box.'

least:1.en: My first night shift started at eleven. The street outside was quiet — no cars, no voices. I expected the *least* exciting job in the world. Then a bicycle crashed into our sandwich board, and a small dog ran inside wearing a tiny hat. The Manager sighed. 'This happens every week.'
least:1.cnHint: 我以为这会是最____刺激的工作，结果第一晚就出了怪事。
least:1.hook: The dog dropped something at my feet and stared up at me.
least:1.line: 'This is the *least* of our problems tonight, trust me.'

least:2.en: The Manager left a note taped to the register: 'Stock the back shelf last.' I did everything else first — mopped, sorted, counted change. The back shelf turned out to hold the *least* interesting items: rubber bands, paper clips, a single sad eraser. But behind the eraser I found a small locked box.
least:2.cnHint: 我把所有其他工作都做完后，发现货架上____重要的东西后面藏着一个上锁的小盒子。
least:2.hook: The box had no key — but it had a name written on it.
least:2.line: 'That shelf has the *least* traffic, so we always check it last.'
